labs_or_tests.evidence_sentence: Her blood analysis showed a severe hypoglycaemia (1.39 mmoL/L), hyponatremia (126 mmoL/L) and hyperkalaemia (6.1 mmoL/L)
Following the identification of significantly high renin level (631.2 mU/L), we introduced a mineralocorticoid replacement therapy with fludrocortisone

Further blood analysis showed low cortisol (< 0.50 nmoL/L), normal renin (44.9 mU/L, normal values 5.5–80 mU/L), low aldosterone levels (26.9 pmoL/L, normal values 138–831 pmol/L) with high ACTH (> 278 pmoL/L)
we repeated all the autoimmunity panels and we found a positivity for thyroid peroxidase (65 kU/L)
we repeated all the autoimmunity panels and we found a positivity for thyroglobulin antibodies (72 UI/mL)
Her adrenal function always remained well-compensated (cortisol 445 nmol/L, ACTH 9.89 pmol/L, renin 59.10 mU/L, aldosterone 41.61 pmol/L)

candidate_mimics.evidence_sentence: Her past medical history was silent except for a recently appeared alopecia and for a familial predisposition for autoimmune thyroid disease
They are both taking levothyroxine treatment. Recently the patient’s twin sister developed an autoimmune thyroiditis with subclinical hypothyroidism that has never needed any replacing therapy.
Nevertheless, a subclinical hypothyroidism was pointed out, with TSH levels (6.64 mU/L) slightly above threshold
leading us to the diagnosis of autoimmune thyroiditis.

final_diagnosis_evidence: High levels of 21-hydroxylase antibodies, significantly high renin level (631.2 mU/L)
